0.0.n: This is the company's name, written in Latin letters.

0.1.n: This indicates a stock company and forms part of the company's full name.

0.2.n: This polite ending identifies the company; the subject is left unstated.

1.0.n: This is the company's name, written in Latin letters.

1.1.n: This indicates a stock company and forms part of the company's full name.

1.2.n: This begins でございます, a more formal alternative to です; it does not mark a location here.

1.3.n: This is the connecting form of ござる, used with で and ます to make a very polite ending.

1.4.n: This attaches to ござい to complete the formal expression でございます.

2.0.n: This is a standard way to refer to yourself; the topic marker は is omitted here.

2.2.n: This is a Japanese family name, given as the speaker's name.

2.3.n: This marks 鈴木 as the name used with 言います.

2.4.n: The polite form of 言う, usually meaning to say, introduces your name in the pattern 名前と言います.

3.0.n: This is a more formal, modest way to refer to yourself than わたし.

3.2.n: This is a Japanese family name, given as the speaker's name.

3.3.n: This marks 鈴木 as the name used with 申します.

3.4.n: This polite form of 申す introduces your name humbly, showing extra respect to the listener.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out the subject when context makes it clear.

1.tip: Treat でございます as one expression: a more formal version of です.

2.tip: Use your name followed by と言います for a standard polite self-introduction.

3.tip: わたくし and と申します make this self-introduction more formal and humble.
